question: Which of the following animals had the most prestigious place in society during the later Vedic period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the later Vedic period, the cow held a prestigious place in society and was considered sacred.
 
• The cow was a symbol of wealth and prosperity, and its ownership was a mark of social status.
 
• Cows were central to the economy; they provided milk, which was a major dietary component, and were used in religious rituals.
 
• The protection of cows was emphasized in the later Vedic texts, and harming a cow was considered a great sin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Later Vedic Period**

 
 
• The later Vedic period is generally considered to be from 1000 BCE to 500 BCE.
 
• It marks the time when the Vedic society started expanding from the northwest of the Indian subcontinent to the Ganges plain.
 
• During this period, the Vedic texts such as the Brahmanas, Aranyakas, and the Upanishads were composed.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Economic Structure**
 
 
• The society was divided into four varnas: Brahmins (priests), Kshatriyas (warriors), Vaishyas (traders and agriculturists), and Shudras (servants).
 
• Agriculture became the main occupation, and the use of iron tools increased agricultural productivity.
 
• Cattle rearing and dairy farming were significant aspects of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Religious Practices**
 
 
• Yajnas (sacrificial rituals) became more elaborate and complex during this period.
 
• The importance of deities like Indra, Agni, and Soma continued, but new gods and goddesses such as Prajapati and Rudra gained prominence.
 
• Cows were often offered in sacrifices and were considered essential for religious ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Cow**
 
 
• The cow was seen as a 'giver' of life and sustenance through its milk, ghee (clarified butter), and other dairy products.
 
• The term 'Gograhana' referred to the act of cow protection or securing cattle, which was a duty of the community.
 
• References to the cow as 'Aghnya' (not to be killed) and 'Kamadhenu' (the cow of plenty) in Vedic texts highlight its revered status.
